chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah from al-Fadl from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a woman, consummated the marriage with her, and she bore him children, then he died. She claimed a portion of her dowry from his heirs and sought her inheritance. He said: 'As for the inheritance, she may claim it. As for the dowry, whatever she took from the husband before he entered into her, that is what made his private part permissible to her, whether little or much. If she received it, accepted it, and he entered into her, she has nothing more after that.'
ai.seo_question: What are a wife's rights to dowry and inheritance if her husband dies after consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that upon consummation, the wife is entitled to her inheritance share and retains the specific dowry portion received prior to the husband's entry into her chamber, as this amount is considered fully settled for the right of intimacy. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the dowry as a contractual right and inheritance as a post-death entitlement, ensuring that the wife does not claim additional dowry for the period between consummation and death. The narration underscores the principle that acceptance of the dowry coupled with consummation finalizes the financial transaction regarding the mahr.
